d: Users can turn the cooktop on/off via the App.
Users can set the power level for each cooking zone via the App.
Users can set a countdown timer to turn off the cooktop via the App, accurate to 1 minute.
Users can lock the physical buttons on the cooktop via the App.
Users can enable Booster mode on the App for each cooking zone.
The App provides preset cooking modes — users just tap one and the cooktop automatically sets the power level and cooking time.
Users can create their own cooking modes in the App, with the following details:
- Mode name
- Power level
- Cooking time
- Number of cooking steps.
When the user leaves home without turning off the cooktop (phone loses Bluetooth connection with the cooktop), they receive an alert from the App.
Alert methods: vibration, sound alert, system notification, in-App notification (if the App is open).
When the cooktop encounters an error, it notifies the App:
- E0: No pot detected warning. Shown as a toast in the App.
- E1: Low voltage warning. Shown as a toast in the App.
- E2: High voltage warning. Shown as a toast in the App.
- E3: Cooktop surface overheating warning. Shown as a toast in the App & vibration.
- E4: Circuit overheating warning. Shown as a toast in the App & vibration.
- E5: Water overflow warning. Shown as a toast in the App, vibration, sound alert, and system notification.

f: Alert when cooktop is on with no timer set
d: Alerts when the cooktop is on but no timer has been set.

f: Alert when cooktop is on with no timer set
d: Alert method: a persistent hint shown on the App screen; if there is no interaction between the user and the cooktop/App for 15 minutes, the phone vibrates once.
Users can choose to turn each of the above alert types on or off.

Users can set a PIN code for the cooktop's control screen. Once set, using the cooktop requires entering the PIN or using the phone's biometric authentication to unlock. The lock re-activates when exiting the control screen or when the screen turns off.
Tracks the cooktop's daily power consumption.

When the cooktop is turned on, the App automatically sends a command to turn on the range hood (if on the same Livotec ecosystem) and syncs the shutoff when the cooktop turns off — no need for two separate actions.

f: Oil temperature sensor to prevent burning
d: The cooktop automatically warns and reduces power when oil temperature exceeds a safe threshold (around 200°C), preventing smoking or burnt oil while frying.
The App immediately notifies when a non-magnetic pot or an incompatible pot base is placed on the cooktop, preventing the cooktop from turning on without receiving heat.

f: Merge 2 zones into 1 large zone (Flex Zone)
d: Users can merge 2 adjacent cooking zones into one large zone via the App to use large pots/pans, griddles, or rectangular cookware.
Turn on/off an LED lighting effect around the base of the pot that mimics a gas flame, helping users transitioning from gas stoves easily gauge the heat level in use.
Users can save 2-3 frequently used power levels and swipe on the cooktop surface (or quick-select in the App) to switch levels without adjusting up/down one notch at a time.

f: Send recipes directly from the App to the cooktop
d: The App suggests recipes by dish; users tap "Cook Now" and the App sends the full sequence of power levels and step timings to the cooktop, which runs the recipe automatically.

After turning off the cooktop, the App and cooktop surface display "H" (very hot, avoid touching) or "h" (still warm, can be used to keep food warm), and the indicator turns off automatically once the surface has cooled to a safe temperature.
The cooktop automatically turns off if a cooking zone runs continuously at the same level for too long with no adjustment, in case the user forgets to monitor it.
Integrates with Google Assistant / Amazon Alexa to turn the cooktop on/off, set timers, or check cooktop status via voice command through a smart speaker.
The App automatically checks for and installs new firmware for the cooktop over Wi-Fi, without needing to bring the cooktop to a service center, and without losing saved settings.
Users set their region's off-peak electricity hours; the App reminds or automatically suggests shifting a scheduled cook (for timer-based dishes) to a cheaper time window.
The App aggregates power consumption by day/week/month as charts, comparing with the previous month so users can track usage trends.
- Immediate in-App alert when power consumption rises abnormally (>30% above the last 7-day average), suggesting the user check their cooking habits or the cooktop's condition.

f: Built-in scale on the cooktop surface
d: Place ingredients on the cooktop surface and the load sensor measures the weight, displaying it directly in the App — useful for precise measurements per a recipe.

Users set up a sequence of steps (e.g., Step 1 - boil at level 9 for 3 minutes → Step 2 - lower to level 3 and simmer for 20 minutes); the cooktop automatically moves through the steps in order without the user needing to watch over it.
The App tracks usage hours and reminds users to clean the glass surface and periodically check the cooling fan to maintain performance and lifespan.

f: Sync cooking modes across multiple cooktops at home
d: Users with multiple Livotec cooktops (e.g., main + secondary) can copy a custom cooking mode from one cooktop to another with a single action in the App.

f: Remote diagnostics & send logs to support
d: When the cooktop reports an error, the App lets users send the activity log directly to Livotec's customer support team to diagnose remotely before dispatching a technician.

f: Recipe suggestions based on available ingredients
d: Users quickly enter a few ingredients they have on hand; the App suggests suitable dishes with a recipe that can be sent directly to the cooktop to cook.
The App automatically reduces power gradually once it detects the dish is boiling/cooked through, maintaining stable heat instead of keeping a high level that wastes electricity.
Based on the dish type, cooking time, and ingredient weight (if used with the built-in scale), the App provides a reference calorie estimate for the dish just cooked.
Users can schedule the cooktop to automatically lock during a fixed time window each day (e.g., after 9 PM, children's bedtime) without manually enabling child lock each time.
When "Guest Mode" is enabled in the App, the cooktop automatically caps the maximum selectable power level, suited for homes with young children or elderly users.

g: Top 5 Breakthrough Features (not yet on the market)
d: Users declare their home's total breaker/CB capacity once during setup. When cooking on multiple zones at once and total power is about to exceed the threshold, the App automatically lowers power on secondary zones while keeping the zone marked "Priority" (e.g., a zone that needs high heat for frying) unchanged — preventing the breaker from tripping without the user having to manage it manually. The market currently only offers fixed Power Management by zone pairs; no brand yet calculates based on the home's actual total capacity and the user's chosen context-based priority.

g: Top 5 Breakthrough Features (not yet on the market)
d: The App recognizes each pot/pan by its size and position on the cooktop, saving a separate "profile" for it: commonly used power level, cooking time, and dishes usually cooked with that pot. Next time the same pot is placed on the cooktop, the App proactively suggests "Fry eggs like last time?" or "Simmer bone broth for 45 minutes?" — just tap once to start. No induction cooktop app currently remembers and suggests based on a specific pot.

g: Top 5 Breakthrough Features (not yet on the market)
d: The App displays the real-time cost of electricity being used (based on EVN's time-of-use tariff or a rate the user enters), warns before peak hours begin, and suggests switching to a saving mode or rescheduling cooking. If "Maximum Saving" mode is enabled, the App can automatically ease power slightly during peak hours. Unlike ordinary energy statistics (viewed only after the fact), this feature calculates cost live while cooking and actively optimizes against Vietnam's real electricity tariff — no brand has gone this far yet.

g: Top 5 Breakthrough Features (not yet on the market)
d: Combines heat and vibration sensors to detect early signs of an imminent boil-over, going beyond simply lowering heat or shutting off like the existing water-overflow alert. After the user finishes wiping up, the App proactively suggests "Continue cooking for 5 more minutes on low" or automatically switches to keep-warm mode. The App keeps a history of boil-over incidents per dish, gradually learning which dishes tend to boil over and lowering the heat earlier on the next cook. The market currently only offers simple shutoff/heat-reduction, with no "recovery" mechanism that learns cooking habits.

g: Top 5 Breakthrough Features (not yet on the market)
d: Connects to Google Calendar/Apple Calendar or a family calendar in the App, automatically suggesting a start-cooking time based on when family members are expected home and how many people are eating tonight — for example, auto-scheduling a soup to start simmering at 5:30 PM to be ready right at 6:30 PM dinner time. Includes a "pre-cook and smart keep-warm" mode that adjusts based on the dish's actual temperature rather than a fixed keep-warm setting. No induction cooktop app currently integrates this deeply with a family calendar to proactively plan cooking.
